java.title: Weekday or weekend? (switch expression)
java.task:
Java 14 made `switch` an **expression**: it produces a value, uses `->` arrows and needs no `break`.

Write `dayType(String day)`:
- `SATURDAY` or `SUNDAY` gives `Weekend`
- `MONDAY` to `FRIDAY` gives `Weekday`
- anything else gives `Unknown`

Use one `return switch (day) { ... };` and no `if`.
java.hint: Several labels can share one arrow: `case "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY" -> "Weekend";` and `default -> "Unknown";` catches the rest.

java.title: A rectangle as a record
java.task:
Records (final in Java 16) are data classes in one line: constructor, getters, `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` come free.

Complete `record Rect(int w, int h)`:
- a **compact constructor** that throws `IllegalArgumentException("size must be positive")` when `w` or `h` is zero or negative
- a method `int area()` that returns `w * h`
java.hint: A compact constructor has no parameter list: `Rect { if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("size must be positive"); }`. The fields `w` and `h` are assigned for you after it.

java.title: Sealed shapes and pattern matching
java.task:
A **sealed** interface lists exactly which types may implement it (final in Java 17), and `instanceof` can test and cast in one step (Java 16).

`Shape` is sealed with two records, `Circle(double r)` and `Square(double side)`.
Write `area(Shape s)` using `instanceof` patterns (`s instanceof Circle c`) and return the area. A circle is `Math.PI * r * r`.
java.hint: `if (s instanceof Circle c) return Math.PI * c.r() * c.r();` then do the same for `Square`. The last `throw` is only there because the compiler cannot see the interface is sealed inside an `if` chain.

java.title: Make two equal points one set entry
java.task:
A `HashSet` finds duplicates with `hashCode()` first and `equals()` second. Right now `Point` uses the default identity versions, so two points with the same `x` and `y` count as different.

Override **both** methods in `Point` so that points with equal `x` and `y` are equal, have the same hash code, and a `Point` is never equal to `null`.
java.hint: `equals`: return true if `o == this`; if `o instanceof Point p`, compare `x == p.x && y == p.y`; otherwise false. `hashCode`: `Objects.hash(x, y)`.

java.title: One max() for any comparable type
java.task:
Write a generic method `maxOf` that returns the largest element of a list, whatever the element type (numbers, strings...), as long as the elements can be compared.

If the list is empty, throw `NoSuchElementException`.
java.hint: The signature is already there: `<T extends Comparable<T>>` says "T must be able to compare itself". Keep the best so far in a variable and use `item.compareTo(best) > 0`.

java.title: Throw, catch and always clean up
java.task:
Two jobs:

1. In `readAge`, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with the message `age must be a number: <text>` when the text is not a whole number, and `age out of range: <n>` when the number is below 0 or above 150.
2. In `main`, wrap the call so a bad input prints `error: <message>` instead of crashing, and a `finally` block prints `checked <text>` after **every** input, good or bad.
java.hint: `Integer.parseInt` throws `NumberFormatException` (a kind of `IllegalArgumentException`) on bad text; catch it and throw your own message. In `main`: `try { ... } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { ... } finally { ... }`.
expect: error: age must be a number: abc

java.title: Count the words, sorted
java.task:
Write `countWords(String text)` that returns how many times each word appears.

- compare words ignoring upper/lower case (`Hello` and `hello` are the same word)
- words are runs of letters; punctuation and spaces only separate them
- return a `TreeMap` so the words come out in alphabetical order
java.hint: `text.toLowerCase().split("[^a-z]+")` gives the words (skip empty strings; the first piece can be empty). `map.merge(word, 1, Integer::sum)` counts in one line.

java.title: Fix the lost updates
java.task:
Four threads each add 1000 to a shared counter, so the answer must be **4000**. `increment()` reads the value, gives other threads a chance to run (this just makes the unlucky timing easy to see), then writes it back, so updates get lost.

Make `Counter` thread-safe. Either `synchronized` or an `AtomicInteger` works; do not remove the `Thread.yield()` line.
java.hint: Reading and writing as two steps is the bug. `synchronized` on the method makes the whole read-yield-write one step for everyone; `AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet()` does the same in a single atomic operation (then the yield is not needed at all).

java.title: Names through a stream
java.task: Write `shout(List<String> names)` with one stream pipeline: keep names with **4 or more** letters, turn them to UPPER CASE, sort them alphabetically, and join them with `", "`.

java.title: Days between and day of the week
java.task:
Use `java.time` (never `Date` or `Calendar`) to write:

- `daysBetween(from, to)`: the number of days from one ISO date (`2024-01-01`) to another
- `weekdayOf(date)`: the day of the week as text, such as `FRIDAY`
java.hint: `LocalDate.parse("2024-01-01")` reads an ISO date. `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(a, b)` counts the days. `date.getDayOfWeek()` returns an enum; `.toString()` gives the name.

java.title: Build a tiny IoC container
java.task:
Spring's container creates your objects and hands them their dependencies. Build the smallest version of that idea.

`Container` needs two methods:
- `register(type, factory)`: remember how to build a `type`
- `get(type)`: build it the **first** time and return that same object every time after (a singleton). If nothing was registered, throw `IllegalStateException("No bean of type <SimpleName>")`

The factory of `Service` asks the container for its `Repo`, which is dependency injection by hand.
java.hint: Keep two maps: `Map<Class<?>, Supplier<?>> factories` and `Map<Class<?>, Object> singletons`. In `get`: `singletons.computeIfAbsent` is tempting, but a factory that calls `get` again would modify the map while it is being computed, so check, build, then `put`.

java.title: A logging proxy, the way AOP works
java.task:
Spring AOP wraps your bean in a **proxy** that runs extra code around each call. Build one by hand with `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`.

Write `logged(iface, target)` so every call on the returned object prints `before <method name>`, then calls the real method, then prints `after <method name>`, and returns the real result.
java.hint: `Proxy.newProxyInstance(iface.getClassLoader(), new Class<?>[] { iface }, (proxy, method, args) -> { ... })`. Inside, call `method.invoke(target, args)` and return what it gives back.

java.title: Sign and verify a token by hand
java.task:
A JWT is three Base64URL parts joined by dots: `header.payload.signature`. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of `header.payload` with a secret key.

Write:
- `sign(payloadJson, secret)`: returns the token. The header is always `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}`. Use Base64URL **without padding**.
- `verify(token, secret)`: returns `true` only if the signature matches the first two parts. A token whose payload was edited must fail.
java.hint: `Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256"); mac.init(new SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(UTF_8), "HmacSHA256")); byte[] sig = mac.doFinal(data.getBytes(UTF_8));` and `Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(bytes)`. To verify, sign the first two parts again and compare with `MessageDigest.isEqual` (constant-time).

java.title: Page numbers vs a cursor
java.task:
`all` is a sorted list of ids: `10, 20, ... 100`. Write both styles of pagination:

- `page(all, page, size)`: page-number style. Pages start at **1**. A page past the end is an empty list.
- `after(all, lastId, limit)`: cursor style. Return up to `limit` ids that are **greater than** `lastId`.
java.hint: `page`: skip `(page - 1) * size` items and take `size` (careful when the skip is past the end). `after`: stream, `filter(id -> id > lastId)`, `limit(limit)`.

java.title: An LRU cache in a few lines
java.task:
A cache must not grow forever. An **LRU** (least recently used) cache throws away the entry nobody has touched for the longest time once it is full.

Make `LruCache` hold at most `capacity` entries. Reading an entry (`get`) counts as using it.

In the test the capacity is 2: after `a` and `b` are added, `a` is read, so adding `c` must evict `b`.
java.hint: `LinkedHashMap` can keep entries in access order: `super(16, 0.75f, true)`. Then override `removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<K,V> eldest)` and return `size() > capacity`. The class below extends `LinkedHashMap` for you.

java.title: Never go over the limit (compare-and-set)
java.task:
`incrementIfBelow(n, max)` must add 1 to `n` only while it is below `max`, and tell the caller whether it did.

Right now it **checks**, then **acts**; another thread can sneak in between (the `Thread.yield()` makes that gap easy to hit). Eight threads try 100 times each against a limit of 500, so the final value must be **exactly 500**, never more.

Rewrite it as a loop with `compareAndSet`, which only succeeds if nobody changed the value since you read it.
java.hint: `while (true) { int cur = n.get(); if (cur >= max) return false; if (n.compareAndSet(cur, cur + 1)) return true; }` If the compare fails, someone else won the race: loop and read again.

java.title: Producer and consumer with a blocking queue
java.task:
A producer thread puts the numbers 1 to 5 into a small queue (room for 2), then puts `-1` as a "no more work" signal. The queue is already filled for you.

Write the **consumer** in `main`: keep taking numbers from the queue and add them up until you receive `-1`, then print `sum=<total>`.
java.hint: `queue.take()` waits when the queue is empty, so no polling or `sleep` is needed. Loop: `int n = queue.take(); if (n == -1) break; sum += n;`.

java.title: Sum of squares on a thread pool
java.task:
Write `sumOfSquares(n)`: add up `1*1 + 2*2 + ... + n*n`, but compute each square as a separate task on a fixed pool of 4 threads.

Submit all tasks, collect the answers from the `Future`s, and **shut the pool down** before returning (a pool that is never shut down keeps the program alive).
java.hint: Build a `List<Callable<Long>>`, call `pool.invokeAll(tasks)`, then `future.get()` for each and add them up. Put `pool.shutdown()` in a `finally`.

java.title: Combine two async calls, with a fallback
java.task:
`price()` and `rate()` each run in the background and return a `CompletableFuture<Double>`.

1. `total()`: start both, **combine** their results when both are ready (`price * rate`), and format it as `Total: 236.00`. Do not block with `get()` or `join()` inside it.
2. `withFallback(f)`: return a future that gives `-1` if `f` failed, or `f`'s own value if it worked.
java.hint: `price().thenCombine(rate(), (p, r) -> p * r).thenApply(t -> String.format("Total: %.2f", t))`. For the fallback: `f.exceptionally(e -> -1)`.
